title: Oscar and the Inheritance
premise: Wren Sandoval, the night dispatcher who has quietly archived two decades of Halloway's secrets, receives a letter confessing to the twenty-year-old murder of Judge Alma Reyes—signed by a man who died in prison three years ago. A second letter arrives promising the 'full file' to whoever can find it first, and Wren realizes the killer is someone using her own dispatch logs to track the investigation. As she lays a trap through manipulated call assignments, she discovers the confessor is the dead man's daughter, protecting the true killer: the retired police captain who built the original case file. In the final confrontation at the records annex, Wren chooses truth over the town's fragile peace, broadcasting the evidence on the taxi company's own radio channel before the captain can silence her.
about_author: E. M. Sterling is the pen name of a former municipal court clerk who spent fifteen years transcribing small-town depositions before turning to fiction. Sterling writes mysteries about the people who keep records—and the records that keep people.

chapters.title: The Night Shift Alphabet
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. We meet her ordered world: the dispatch desk, the filing cabinets, the town that calls her at 3 a.m. and never learns her name. A letter arrives postmarked the day Judge Reyes died, confessing to her murder in another man's handwriting. The emotional beat is the first crack in twenty years of controlled invisibility.

chapters.title: Signed by a Dead Man
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. She verifies that Dale Pruitt, the confessed killer, died in prison three years ago. A second letter arrives: 'The full file goes to whoever finds it first. You already know where.' She recognizes the phrasing—it echoes her own dispatch shorthand. Beat: fear sharpening into professional obsession.

chapters.title: The Captain's Cold Case
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, with flashback. She pulls her archived logs from the night of the murder and finds gaps—calls erased from the tape, all signed out by Captain Harlan Voss, the investigating officer. She visits him; he's charming, helpful, and knows too much about her filing system. Beat: dread disguised as nostalgia.

chapters.title: What the Logs Remember
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Wren and Voss. Voss, aware someone is pulling old records, begins using the taxi company's calls to monitor Wren's movements. Wren enlists her driver, Marcus, a Pruitt family friend, who reveals Pruitt had a daughter, Lila, who visits his grave monthly. Beat: loyalty tested as Marcus must choose between Wren and the Pruitt name.

chapters.title: Lila Pruitt's Confession
chapters.summary: Lila's POV. Lila wrote the letters: her father died insisting he was innocent, and she found his hidden notes implicating Voss. She sent them to Wren because the dispatch logs were the only untampered record. But someone followed her to the mailbox. Beat: grief curdling into terror as she realizes Voss is hunting the file through her.

chapters.title: Dispatch, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Voss requests a taxi—Wren recognizes the trap and sends Marcus instead, feeding false destinations through the radio to map how Voss tracks calls. She confirms he has a copy of her dispatch codes. The beat is cold fury: the violation of the one system she trusted to keep her invisible.

chapters.title: The File in the Annex
chapters.summary: Wren and Lila's POV, alternating. Following Pruitt's notes, they locate the original evidence file hidden in the records annex—photos, a witness statement Voss buried, and a tape of the erased calls. But the annex alarm has already been tripped once this month. Beat: triumph undercut by the certainty they are expected.

chapters.title: Every Road Leads to You
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. He confronts Wren at the dispatch desk, offering her the thing she's always wanted—recognition, a name on a commendation—in exchange for the file. He reveals he erased the logs to protect the town, not himself: the killer was the judge's own protégé, now a sitting official. Beat: temptation, and Wren's refusal.

chapters.title: The Open Channel
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Climax. Voss comes to destroy the annex file; Wren has already moved it. She lures him into confessing on an open radio channel while Marcus drives the town's night callers as witnesses, then broadcasts the tape and the protégé's name across the frequency. Voss corners her in the records room. Beat: terror transfigured into the courage of the invisible.

chapters.title: Filed Under Truth
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, weeks later. Voss is arrested; the protégé's case reopens; Lila clears her father's name. The town knows Wren Sandoval's name now, and she finds she can bear it. She reorganizes the files—not alphabetized by secrecy, but by date of truth. Final beat: quiet justice, and a dispatcher who finally goes off shift.
